explanation: The Santhal Hool broke out on 30 June 1855 at Bhognadih, when Sidhu and Kanhu Murmu called the Santhals of the Damin-i-Koh to rise against zamindars, mahajans and Company revenue officials. It was crushed by 1856, after which the British carved out the separate Santhal Parganas district and exempted it from ordinary regulations. The earlier dates are traps for the Kol uprising (1831-32) and the Rangpur-era disturbances; the Munda Ulgulan under Birsa Munda came much later, in 1899-1900.

In the MBSE HSSLC results declared in 2024 the commerce stream recorded 79.60% passes, placing it just below arts (79.71%) and well above science (72.69%). The tempting distractor is the figure close to the overall HSSLC pass percentage, which was 78.04% (9,227 of about 11,824 candidates). Commerce topper that year was David Lalhminghlua with 460 marks.

On 3 June 2024 the Department of School Education and Literacy signed the MoU with the National Book Trust, India, which sits under the Department of Higher Education, to build the institutional framework for Rashtriya e-Pustakalaya. NBT was the natural partner because the platform is about non-academic reading material: over 1,000 titles from 40-plus publishers at launch, scaling to 10,000 books in 100-plus languages, graded into the four NEP 2020 age bands (3-8, 8-11, 11-14, 14-18). INFLIBNET is the standard trap here, but its digital libraries (Shodhganga, e-ShodhSindhu) serve higher education, not school readers.

IIT Jodhpur researchers, led by Dr Deepika Bhattu, published the study in Nature Communications in May 2024 under the title on local incomplete combustion emissions defining PM2.5 oxidative potential in Northern India. The key finding was that the health damage is driven less by total PM mass than by the oxidative potential of organic aerosols from incomplete burning of biomass and fossil fuels, including traffic exhaust, with ammonium chloride a dominant component inside Delhi. IIT Delhi and IIT Kanpur also run well-known Delhi air-quality programmes, which is why they read as plausible options.

The MEA announced on 30 May 2024 that Ravi Shankar, a 1995-batch IFS officer then serving as Additional Secretary, would be the next Ambassador to Ukraine; he took charge in Kyiv in August 2024, shortly before PM Modi's visit. The appointment came just ahead of the Ukraine peace summit in Switzerland. Harsh Kumar Jain is the classic trap, because he was the outgoing Ambassador to Ukraine whom Ravi Shankar replaced.

Prof. Lalbiakdiki Hnamte of Mizoram University was made Working Chairman of the Mizoram Education Reforms Committee constituted on 21 February 2024, with R. Lalthanmawia as Member Secretary. The trap is Dr. Vanlalthlana: as Education Minister he heads the committee as Chairman, not Working Chairman. Dr. Tawnenga and Prof. Vanlalhruaii were included as ordinary members, which is why all four names look right.

Sikkim became the first Northeastern state to bring back the Old Pension Scheme, announced by Chief Minister Prem Singh Tamang on 9 February 2024 at Rangpo, extending the Sikkim Services (Pension) Rules, 1990 to employees appointed on or after 1 April 2006. Roughly 30,000 state employees stood to benefit, and the move came weeks before the 2024 assembly election. Rajasthan, Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, Punjab and Himachal had already reverted to OPS, but none of them is in the Northeast.

The Ministry of Information and Broadcasting took the award for Best Performance in Accounts for 2023-24. These awards are given by the Controller General of Accounts on Civil Accounts Day, observed on 1 March to mark the foundation of the Indian Civil Accounts Service in 1976. Ministry of Finance is the intuitive but wrong pick, since it administers the accounting system rather than competing for the performance prize.

The base year supplies the constant set of prices used to value output, and valuing current output at those constant prices gives real GDP. Nominal GDP by definition uses current-year prices, so the two options mentioning nominal GDP are the traps. India's national accounts currently use 2011-12 as the base year, with a revision to 2022-23 announced by MoSPI.

For revision, the standard figures are: services (tertiary) contribute roughly 54% of India's gross value added, industry (secondary) about 25-30%, and agriculture (primary) about 18%, so services are the largest contributor while the secondary sector is second. The official key for this paper marks the secondary sector, so note the key's answer for scoring purposes but carry the sectoral shares above into the exam hall, since that is what every other question on this topic will test.
disputeNote: The official key marks 'Secondary Sector', but the tertiary/services sector is by a wide margin the largest contributor to India's GDP (about 54% of GVA versus roughly 25-30% for industry). Either the key is wrong or the printed option order differs from what was extracted.

explanation: R.K. Shanmukham Chetty, independent India's first Finance Minister, presented the first budget on 26 November 1947; it was an interim budget covering only about seven and a half months to 31 March 1948 and contained no new taxes. John Mathai is the standard trap: he succeeded Chetty and presented the first budget of the Republic of India in 1950, the one that announced the Planning Commission. Jawaharlal Nehru did present a budget, but much later, in 1958.

State Bank of India is by far the largest commercial bank in India on every measure that matters for the exam: total assets, deposits, branch network and employees. It traces back to the Imperial Bank of India and was constituted in its present form under the SBI Act, 1955, with the RBI as majority holder until the government took over that stake in 2008. Among the options, ICICI is the largest private bank and PNB the second-largest public sector bank, but neither approaches SBI's balance sheet.

Indira Gandhi coined 'Garibi Hatao' during the 1971 Lok Sabha campaign, and poverty removal was then written in as the central objective of the Fifth Five-Year Plan (1974-79), whose twin aims were 'removal of poverty' and 'attainment of self-reliance'. The plan was drafted under D.P. Dhar and was terminated a year early, in 1978, by the Janata government. The Third Plan is the trap because it is the other famous Nehru-era plan, but its focus was self-sufficiency in foodgrains and heavy industry.

Prof. C.N.R. Rao, a solid-state and materials chemist at JNCASR Bengaluru, is called the father of Indian nanotechnology for his work on nanomaterials and for steering the Nano Mission; he received the Bharat Ratna in 2014. C.V. Raman is the tempting distractor because he is India's best-known physicist, but his Nobel-winning work on light scattering predates nanoscience by decades. Ramanujan was a mathematician and Amartya Sen an economist.

National Technology Day is observed on 11 May, marking 11 May 1998, when India conducted the Pokhran-II nuclear tests, test-fired the Trishul missile and flew the indigenous Hansa-3 aircraft on the same day. Prime Minister Atal Bihari Vajpayee declared the day, and it has been observed since 1999 with a theme announced by the Technology Development Board. Do not confuse it with National Science Day on 28 February, which commemorates the discovery of the Raman Effect.

Cyrtodactylus vairengtensis is a bent-toed gecko described in November 2023 and named after Vairengte in Kolasib district, where it was collected; the genus Cyrtodactylus is the giveaway, since it is a large radiation of bent-toed geckos concentrated in Northeast India and Southeast Asia. Mizoram has yielded several new Cyrtodactylus species in recent years, making the state a hotspot for herpetological description. The place-name suffix -ensis in the species epithet is the standard clue that the animal is named after a locality.

Dr Lalji Singh developed DNA fingerprinting in India, using the Bkm-derived Bnd 2 probe at CCMB Hyderabad, and the technique was first accepted as evidence by an Indian court in 1989. He is remembered as the father of Indian DNA fingerprinting, later headed CCMB and served as Vice-Chancellor of BHU, and received the Padma Shri in 2004. DNA barcoding and whole-genome sequencing are later, distinct technologies used mainly for species identification and full genome reading rather than individual identification in casework.

Brucethoa isro, a parasitic deep-sea isopod found in the gill chamber of the Indian mackerel, was described by researchers working off the Kerala coast near Kollam and named to honour ISRO. Naming marine discoveries after Indian institutions has become a pattern in recent Kerala-based taxonomy, which is why the state is the answer rather than the space agency's home state of Karnataka. Karnataka is the trap precisely because ISRO's headquarters are in Bengaluru.

Rashmi is the humanoid built by Ranchi-based software engineer Ranjit Srivastava, billed as the world's first Hindi-speaking lip-syncing humanoid robot, which also handles Bhojpuri, Marathi and English. Shalu is the trap: it is a separate Indian humanoid, made from waste material by Dinesh Patel at IIT Bombay and able to speak dozens of languages. Sophia is Hanson Robotics' Hong Kong-built humanoid and Mitra is the Bengaluru-made greeter robot from Invento Robotics, so neither is Indian-invented in the sense the question wants.

Lemlawi is the Mizo mouth-harp, a small plucked instrument held against the lips so that the mouth cavity acts as the resonator, and it belongs with the familiar list of Mizo instruments such as Tumphit, Phenglawng, Rawchhem, Buhchangkuang and the darkhuang gong. The other three options are ordinary Mizo nouns rather than instruments, with Berhbu in particular meaning a weaver-bird's nest. When in doubt on this pattern of question, look for the term that appears in standard listings of Mizo folk instruments.

Saphun was the ritual by which a person abandoned the sakhua of his own clan and took on the religion of another clan, involving a sacrifice performed by a priest of the adopting clan. It mattered socially because sakhua defined clan identity and the obligations that came with it, so saphun effectively transferred a household's religious allegiance. Sakung, the main house-post associated with clan sacrifices, is the near-miss distractor.

Ahmangaihi Khiangte won the Mizo Academy of Letters Book of the Year 2023 for her debut work Pangparhnima, receiving a citation and a cash award of Rs 10,000 when the prize was announced in April 2024; she is among the youngest authors ever to take the award. MAL picks one best Mizo-language book each year, and roughly 170 Mizo titles were published in 2023. Lalhruaitluanga Chawngte is the trap, having won an earlier edition of the same award for Aizawlah Aizawler.

Mizoram's state animal is the Saza, the serow (Capricornis sumatraensis), a goat-antelope of steep forested slopes that is Schedule I protected. Sakei, the tiger, is the obvious trap because it is the national animal, while Sazuk is the sambar deer. Pair this with the state bird, Vavu (Mrs Hume's pheasant), and the state tree, Herhse (Indian rosewood), since MPSC tends to rotate these three.

Fungki is the powder flask made from a hollowed bison or mithun horn, carried with the flintlock musket along with the shot pouch as part of a Mizo hunter's kit. The horn was chosen because it is naturally watertight and would keep gunpowder dry in the hills. Sahmim is a food preparation and Paitung a bamboo tube, so neither belongs to hunting equipment.

A.G. McCall, Superintendent of the Lushai Hills through the 1930s and early 1940s, wrote Lushai Chrysalis, the administrator's account of Mizo society in transition that remains a standard source. N.E. Parry, also a Superintendent, is the trap because he wrote A Monograph on Lushai Customs and Ceremonies and The Lakhers. Remember McCall too for the village-administration reforms and the Circle Interpreter system introduced during his tenure.

Dr Peter Fraser, the Welsh Presbyterian medical missionary who arrived in 1908, took up the cause of the bawi and pressed the colonial administration to end the institution, bringing him into open conflict with the Superintendent and with fellow missionaries who thought the system benign. His campaign led to bawi being allowed to redeem their freedom and eventually to the practice dying out. J. Shakespeare, who as Superintendent had defended the system as a form of chiefly welfare, is the natural trap.

Hmui is the Mizo spinning wheel used to twist raw cotton into yarn, the step that precedes weaving on the loin loom. It sits in the traditional textile sequence with cotton cleaning and the loom parts, which is why the loom-related term Suvel is the tempting distractor here. Yarn spun on the hmui was what supplied the puan weaving that Mizoram is known for.

Capt. L.Z. Sailo (Lalzuala Sailo, born 1924 at Sialhawk) was the first Mizo to receive the Padma Bhushan, conferred in 2007; a former Army Medical Corps officer, he was better known as an author and songwriter, and his Runlum Nuthai took the Mizo Academy of Letters Book of the Year in 2002. Brig. T. Sailo, the former Chief Minister, is the standard trap because he is the more famous Sailo, but his civilian honour was the Padma Shri. Watch the surname: MPSC often pairs the two Sailos in the same option set.

Khuallam, literally the dance of the guests, is also called Thingdim; it is performed by visiting guests entering the arena at the Khuangchawi, the feast of merit, with each dancer draped in a puandum and moving to the beat of the darbu. Chai and Chawnglaizawn are separate Mizo dances tied to Chapchar Kut and to mourning respectively, and Solakia is a warrior dance, so all three are wrong here. Remember the pairing Khuallam = Thingdim as a straight recall item.

The pair is built from two opposite runs of the alphabet: the first letters move forward A, B, C, so the next is D, while the second letters move backward Z, Y, X, so the next is W. That gives DW. Equivalently, each pair is a letter and its mirror image (A pairs with Z, B with Y, C with X, D with W), since the positions in every pair add up to 27.

This tests Hohfeld's jural correlatives, the standard jurisprudence pairs: a right in one person implies a duty in another, and in exactly the same way a power in one person implies a liability in another. So Power corresponds to Liability, not to any of the mere opposites offered. The opposite-style distractors (Powerless, Weak) fail because Right and Duty are not opposites either; they are two sides of the same legal relation.

Every term is a perfect cube plus one: 0 cubed +1 = 1, 1 cubed +1 = 2, 2 cubed +1 = 9, 3 cubed +1 = 28, so the missing term is 4 cubed +1 = 65. The pattern is confirmed by the terms that follow: 5 cubed +1 = 126 and 6 cubed +1 = 217. Whenever a series jumps 1, 2, 9, 28 the gaps grow far too fast for an arithmetic or simple multiplicative rule, so test cubes first.

The differences themselves form an arithmetic sequence increasing by 2: minus 4, minus 6, minus 8, minus 10, minus 12. So 44 minus 4 = 40, 40 minus 6 = 34, 34 minus 8 = 26, and the chain checks out with 26 minus 10 = 16 and 16 minus 12 = 4. The missing term is therefore 26; the given tail values 16 and 4 are what let you confirm the rule rather than guess it.

The intended relation is person-to-defining-quality: a libertine is a person defined by immorality, so the parallel is a person paired with the trait that characterises him, as in miser-selfishness or altruist-selflessness. Note that the printed word 'Immortality' is almost certainly a misprint for 'Immorality', and because more than one option fits the person-plus-defining-quality pattern the question carries no answer in the source data. Treat it as a dropped question rather than one to reason to a single choice.
disputeNote: The source entry has answerIndex -1 and answerLetter null, so no official option is marked. The question is also defective: 'Immortality' appears to be a misprint for 'Immorality', and both (b) miser:selfishness and (c) altruist:selflessness satisfy the person-to-defining-quality relation.

explanation: An author produces a manuscript, which is the preliminary written form of the eventual finished work; the architect produces a blueprint in exactly the same way, a plan that precedes the finished building. Engineer-bridge is the deliberate trap because it pairs a professional with the completed product rather than with the draft or plan. Doctor-stethoscope fails for a different reason: that is a person and his tool, not his output.

A tally is the process of counting votes, so the parallel must be a counting process applied to the thing counted, and a census is precisely the count of a population. Taxation-revenue is the closest trap, but that is a process and its outcome, not a process of counting. Government-administration and team-sports are relations of function and context, not enumeration.

In 'This is what I want', the word 'what' is a relative pronoun standing for 'the thing which'; it does duty twice, as the complement of 'is' and as the object of 'want'. It cannot be an adverb because it is not modifying the verb, and it cannot be a preposition because nothing follows it as an object. This nominal-relative use of 'what' is the one grammar point this question is testing.

Absolve is a verb of releasing or clearing, and with charges, blame or guilt it standardly takes 'from': the court absolved him from all the charges. Compare the same pattern in 'exempt from', 'acquit of', 'free from' and 'release from', all verbs of removal that take 'from' for the thing removed. 'To' and 'upon' are simply ungrammatical with absolve.

Precarious describes something so insecurely held that it is liable to collapse or cause harm, as in a precarious ledge or a precarious financial position, so 'dangerous' captures the element of risk that the word carries. 'Unstable' is the tempting near-synonym, but it describes only a lack of steadiness and drops the sense of consequent peril that is central to precarious. 'Temporary' and 'predictable' miss the meaning entirely, the latter being close to the opposite.

All four pairings are the standard ones: Green Revolution for high-yielding-variety foodgrain production from the mid-1960s under M.S. Swaminathan and Norman Borlaug, Yellow for oilseeds under the Technology Mission on Oilseeds (1986), Round for potato, and Protein for the drive to raise agricultural and protein output announced in the 2014-15 budget as a second green revolution. Since none of the four is misstated, the 'all of the above' option is the answer, and every option that excludes one of them is wrong. Keep the rest of the colour list handy too: White for milk, Blue for fish, Pink for prawn or onion, Golden for horticulture and honey, Silver for eggs.

States that score well on HDI also tend to rank high on the NITI Aayog SDG India Index, Kerala being the standard illustration, so the assertion is true. The reason is true as well and is exactly why the correlation exists: a large share of the 17 SDGs and their targets, notably SDG 3 on health and SDG 4 on education, measure the very dimensions that HDI is built from, alongside income. Because the reason supplies the mechanism behind the assertion rather than being a separate true fact, the correct code is the one saying R explains A.

Agriculture and allied activities still absorb the largest share of India's workforce, roughly 45% by recent Periodic Labour Force Survey estimates, even though the sector produces less than a fifth of GVA. That mismatch between employment share and output share is the classic point about disguised unemployment and low agricultural productivity. Tertiary is the trap because it leads on GDP contribution, not on employment; the public sector is not a sector in this classification at all.

DILRMP is a central sector scheme, meaning the Centre bears 100% of the cost; it was converted to full central funding in 2016 when the earlier National Land Records Modernization Programme, which was centrally sponsored with state cost-sharing, was recast. The programme aims at conclusive land titling through computerised records, digitised cadastral maps, registration integration and the ULPIN or Bhu-Aadhaar identifier. The partial-funding options are traps carried over from the old NLRMP sharing pattern.

Singapore was indeed the largest source of FDI equity inflows into India in 2023-24, and the reason offered is the accepted explanation: once the India-Mauritius tax treaty was amended to remove the capital-gains exemption, Mauritius lost its routing advantage and investment shifted decisively to Singapore, whose own treaty was amended in parallel but which offers a genuine financial-services base. The 2024 protocol adding a principal purpose test tightened the Mauritius route further. Since the reason supplies the actual cause of the shift described in the assertion, the code stating that R correctly explains A is the one to mark.

Fiscal policy is the use of the government's budget, and all three listed items are its components: receipts on the revenue side including taxes, expenditure on the spending side, and public debt as the borrowing that bridges the gap. Since the deficit is financed by borrowing, debt management cannot be separated out from fiscal policy, which is why any option excluding item (iii) fails. Contrast this with monetary policy, which the RBI runs through the repo rate, CRR, SLR and open market operations.

For revision, the mechanics of the MSS, introduced under the 2004 MoU between the Government and the RBI, are these: when large capital or forex inflows leave surplus rupee liquidity in the system, the RBI mops it up by selling government paper, that is by issuing Treasury Bills and dated securities designated as MSS securities, and parks the proceeds in a separate MSS cash account with the RBI so the money is sterilised rather than spent. That segregated account is what distinguishes MSS from ordinary open market operations. Note the key's marked option for scoring, but remember the sterilisation mechanism itself, since that is what any descriptive or follow-up question will test.
disputeNote: The official key marks 'Purchasing Treasury Bills and/or dated securities'. Under the MSS the RBI absorbs excess liquidity by issuing/selling T-Bills and dated securities, not purchasing them; purchasing would inject liquidity. Option (a) 'Issuing Treasury Bills and/or dated securities' is the factually correct method.

explanation: The Public Distribution System dates to 1945, growing out of the wartime rationing introduced under British administration to manage acute food scarcity, and it was retained after independence rather than wound up. It was made universal in the 1960s alongside the creation of the Food Corporation of India and the Agricultural Prices Commission in 1965, which is the source of the tempting 1965 option. Later milestones worth remembering are the Revamped PDS of 1992, the Targeted PDS of 1997 with its APL/BPL split, and the National Food Security Act of 2013.

Iris, unveiled in 2024 at KTCT Higher Secondary School in Thiruvananthapuram, Kerala, is billed as India's first AI teacher robot; it was developed by Makerlabs Edutech in connection with the school's Atal Tinkering Lab and is a generative-AI-driven humanoid that can answer questions across subjects in three languages. Mitra is the standard trap, but it is Invento Robotics' greeter and interaction robot, not a teaching robot. Iris is a robot in sari-clad humanoid form, which is why it drew so much coverage.

Dingdi puan tah and Hrangkhupa se dar are two traditional Mizo names for the same star, both appearing in the standard list of arsi names that the Mizos gave to the stars and constellations they used to mark seasons and jhum-cycle timing. Questions of this type simply pair alternative names within the traditional star nomenclature, so the reliable approach is to memorise the paired names rather than reason them out. The other options are unrelated terms drawn from folklore rather than alternate names for this star.

Zawlpuan phah is the traditional form of betrothal in which the arrangement is sealed by the spreading of the zawlpuan, marking the couple as engaged before the full marriage negotiations and bride-price settlement are completed. It belongs with the other Mizo marriage-related terms an aspirant should keep together, such as palai (the go-between), man (bride price) and thutphah. The other three options are not marriage customs, which is what makes this a straight vocabulary recall.

Puma Zai, the great song movement that began around 1907-08 and spread rapidly through the Lushai Hills, developed into a family of related zai forms, and Hrangchhawni zai, Mutelen zai and Chalmar zai belong to that lineage. Darpawngi zai stands outside it, being the body of song associated with the composer Darpawngi in her own right rather than a branch of the Puma Zai tradition. Remember Puma Zai also for its historical importance as a revival of traditional singing that alarmed the missionaries just before the 1919 revival.

Pu Lalbuaia of the Congress was Mizoram's first Rajya Sabha member, serving from 17 July 1972 to 16 July 1978; the seat came into being when Mizoram was made a Union Territory in January 1972 and got its single seat in the Council of States. Pu Hiphei and Pu C.L. Ruala are the traps here, since both are well-known Mizoram parliamentarians but from the Lok Sabha side or later Rajya Sabha terms. Mizoram has exactly one Rajya Sabha seat and one Lok Sabha seat, a useful fact in itself.

The workable distinction is that sal were war captives taken in raids, treated as chattel who could be held by any household and bought, sold or given away, whereas bawi were dependants who attached themselves to the chief's household and could be possessed only by a chief. Option (a) is the trap because it reverses the two exactly, giving bawi the war-captive origin that belongs to sal. Option (d) is also reversed on the sub-types: Inpuichhung bawi were the destitute taken into the chief's house, Chemsen bawi were those fleeing punishment for bloodshed, and Tuklut bawi were those who surrendered in war.

The statement about R.B. Chawnga being appointed President of the District Council Court at Aizawl is the one that does not hold; the other three describe the first term of the Lushai Hills Autonomous District Council correctly, including Lalsawia as the first Chief Executive Member after the Mizo Union swept the April 1952 election. The Council was inaugurated at Aizawl on 26 April 1952 by Assam Chief Minister Bishnuram Medhi under the Sixth Schedule, and its finances were tiny at the outset, which is why the very small first budget figure is genuine rather than a misprint. Read the stem carefully on this pattern: it asks for the INCORRECT statement, so three of the four options are facts worth learning in their own right.

The differences double each time: 22 minus 16 = 6, 34 minus 22 = 12, 58 minus 34 = 24, 106 minus 58 = 48, so the next difference is 96 and the missing term is 106 plus 96 = 202. The rule is confirmed by the final term, since 202 plus 192 = 394. Equivalently each term is the previous term doubled minus 10, which also gives 2 times 106 minus 10 = 202.
